question: In the unsignalized midblock-crosswalk example in Figure 3B-16, how far in advance of the crosswalk are the yield lines shown?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In the unsignalized midblock-crosswalk example (Drawing B of Figure 3B-16), the yield lines are shown 20 to 50 feet in advance of the crosswalk, together with Yield Here to Pedestrians (R1-5) signs at the same locations. This matches the MUTCD's recommended placement distance for yield lines and R1-5 signs on uncontrolled multi-lane approaches. Guidance (recommended): - "If yield (stop) lines and Yield Here to (Stop Here for) Pedestrians signs are used in advance of a crosswalk that crosses an uncontrolled multi-lane approach, the signs should be placed 20 to 50 feet in advance of the nearest edge of the crosswalk (see Section 3B.19 and Figure 3B-16)." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 3B-16, Drawing B (Unsignalized midblock crosswalk) shows a dimension line labeled "20 to 50 ft" between the yield lines (marked as optional in each lane) and the nearest edge of the crosswalk, with R1-5 signs at the yield-line locations. - [Image 2] The full page view of Figure 3B-16 confirms the same "20 to 50 ft" dimension in Drawing B, and also shows the identical 20-to-50-foot dimension in Drawing C (crosswalk across ramp). - [Image 3] Section 2B.19 text confirms the 20-to-50-foot placement guidance for yield lines and R1-5 signs in advance of the crosswalk, cross-referencing Figure 3B-16. - [Image 4] Figure 2B-2 illustrates the R1-5 series Yield Here To Pedestrians signs that are shown at the yield-line locations in Figure 3B-16. - [Image 5] Figure 3I-1 shows related unsignalized-crosswalk treatments (tubular markers with W11-2 assemblies) but does not add distance information for the yield lines. Citations: - Section 2B.19 Guidance §3 (p.81) - Figure 3B-16 (p.574) - Page 123 - Page 122
gold_answer: 20 to 50 feet in advance of the crosswalk.
